elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any liquidated damages under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause replaces the payment obligation with “Customer shall not be required to pay Vendor any liquidated damages,” and contains no operative liquidated-damages payment duty.

elements.element: Customer is not required to pay any penalties under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause states that Customer shall not be required to pay “any ... penalty under this Agreement” and imposes no penalty.

elements.element: Any liquidated damages payable by Customer are limited to an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause prohibits, rather than imposes, liquidated damages; therefore no non-termination liquidated damages are payable.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed, so the conditional cap requirement is satisfied by the demonstrable absence of such a fee.

elements.element: An early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: No liquidated amount is payable at all, so there is no additional liquidated amount beyond the permitted fallback category.

result.reason: The rendered language removes the original weekly liquidated-damages obligation and imposes no liquidated damages or penalty on Customer, satisfying the preferred position. It also satisfies the fallback restrictions because no early-termination fee or other liquidated amount exists. The change is limited to the targeted remedy and does not add an unrelated requirement. Drafting quality is reduced because the retained late-invoice condition makes the purported agreement-wide prohibition appear conditional, although the clause still contains no operative payment obligation.
